projects.name: MITRE ATT&CK Flashcards
projects.description: I know every red flag in the book. Still need flashcards. Swipe right and test me.
projects.label: Independent cybersecurity learning project
projects.problem: I wanted a way to practice and learn about MITRE ATT&CK techniques and sub-techniques in my spare time, using the best methods available for self-directed learning. I can pick this up for as short as 30 seconds and get something out of it, and the built-in tracking helps me see progress over time.
projects.role: I independently built the learning application as a way to deepen my cybersecurity understanding and make the material easier to revisit.

decisions.purpose: Break a broad cybersecurity framework into focused concepts to study and revisit.
Explore the relationship between ATT&CK terminology and the events involved in threat detection.

delivered: A public cybersecurity learning application for exploring ATT&CK techniques, sub-techniques, security events, and threat detection concepts.

media.title: MITRE ATT&CK Flashcards learning app
media.caption: The live independent learning application. It is a study project, not a production threat detection platform.
media.alt: MITRE ATT&CK Flashcards cybersecurity learning application.

projects.name: Tiny Goose Club
projects.description: A quiet space for people to feel safe to make things at any skill level, talk or not, and get excited with some good old fashioned show-and-tell. I wanted a space like this and din't find one, so I made it myself.
projects.label: Community organizing & creative meetup
projects.problem: Making time for a creative project can be easier with company, especially for neurodivergent people. Tiny Goose Club gives creatives in Baltimore a regular public meetup where they can bring something to work on and get to know one another.
projects.role: I organize and host the biweekly meetup, and built its website to share event information, expectations, and RSVP links.

decisions.decision: A regular gathering open to the public
decisions.purpose: Give people a recurring opportunity to make things and build connections.

decisions.decision: Event information and expectations in one place
decisions.purpose: Help someone new understand the meetup and find a way to join.

delivered: A biweekly public creative meetup in Baltimore that I organize and host.
A public website with meetup information and RSVP links.

media.title: Tiny Goose Club meetup website
media.caption: The live meetup website, with information for people interested in joining the creative gathering.
media.alt: Tiny Goose Club website for a public creative meetup in Baltimore.

projects.name: Medium Talk
projects.description: Enjoying conversational card games, I wanted a way to bring that experience to strangers meeting in a public setting. Medium Talk is a conversation app I built to support a public picnic I hosted in Baltimore.
projects.label: Independent community project
projects.problem: Strangers meeting at a public picnic need a starting point for conversation. I hosted the event through Meetup in a Baltimore park and built an app to support getting to know one another.
projects.role: I organized the picnic and built Medium Talk to support conversation at the event.

decisions.purpose: Give people meeting for the first time a shared starting point.

decisions.decision: A tool connected to an in-person event
decisions.purpose: Support the social setting I was organizing.

delivered: A conversation app, available at mediumtalk.org, built for the public picnic I hosted.

media.title: Medium Talk conversation experience
media.caption: A fan of three Medium Talk screens: the picnic arrival prompt, the central home screen, and a city conversation prompt.
media.alt: Three Medium Talk screens in an overlapping fan: a yellow picnic prompt on the left, the Medium Talk home screen centered in front, and a blue city prompt on the right.

media.title: Picnic arrival prompt
media.caption: A prompt designed to help picnic guests arrive, get grounded, and begin a real conversation.
media.alt: Yellow Medium Talk prompt asking, What are you giving yourself permission not to do today?

media.title: City conversation prompt
media.caption: A city-specific prompt that gives strangers a generous, low-pressure opening question. I generated city-specific color schemes from colors commonly associated with each city, for 12 U.S. cities and 43 cities in total.
media.alt: Blue Medium Talk prompt asking, What is a way someone has loved or supported you that meant everything?

projects.contact: Have an idea that brings people together? Tell me about the setting and how software could help.

projects.role: I built the artist website, including dedicated desktop and mobile experiences. Credits for supplied art, music, and other collaborators still need to be added.

decisions.purpose: Give the artist’s identity room to work at different screen sizes.

decisions.decision: Music and media within the site

projects.name: Kellogg Board Fellows Optimizer
projects.description: I built a tool to match MBA students to ranked corporate board internship spots in a mathematically-optimal way, saving an administrator hours of manual work, and providing proof to students that the matching was fair and unbiased.
projects.label: Original tool / independent refresh planned
projects.problem: The original organizational task was to match fellows to placements using ranked preferences. A matching tool provides a way to work through those preferences and produce placement results.
projects.role: I originally built the tool, which was used in a more rudimentary form. My repository is a fork of the organization’s project. Any future portfolio refresh is independent; it is not presented as commissioned or adopted by Kellogg.

decisions.decision: Ranked preferences as the matching input
decisions.purpose: Base placement matching on the preferences provided.

delivered: The original, more rudimentary matching tool was used. The organization’s repository is linked separately for attribution.
planned: An independent portfolio refresh. It has not been completed or adopted by Kellogg.

media.title: Original matching interface
media.caption: A refreshed interface concept for explaining the preference import, validation, matching, and download workflow. It is independent portfolio work, not represented as a commissioned or adopted Kellogg interface.
media.alt: Kellogg Board Fellows Optimizer interface showing a four-step internship matching workflow.

projects.contact: Working through preferences or placement data by hand? Tell me about the rules and the output you need.

projects.name: Poster Slicer
projects.description: I make things bigger. Yes, your printer can handle it.
projects.label: Independent tool / interface refresh planned
projects.problem: Printing a large image does not always mean using a large-format printer. This tool is for people who want to assemble a poster from ordinary sheets of paper.
projects.role: I built Poster Slicer as an independent tool for turning an image into a printable multi-page poster.

decisions.decision: Split an image across ordinary paper sheets
decisions.purpose: Make a larger poster possible with a standard paper format.

delivered: The current image-to-poster tool is available online.
planned: An interface refresh. Before-and-after comparisons will be added once the refresh exists.

media.caption: The live Poster Slicer interface showing image upload, poster dimensions, page count, and a multi-page preview.
media.alt: Poster Slicer interface with a large script image divided across a printable grid of pages.

projects.contact: Have a repetitive image or document task? Tell me about your inputs and the finished output you need.

projects.name: RekordBox Bass Notes
projects.description: I know exactly which tracks will make you feel it in your hips. Your downstairs neighbors already hate me.
projects.label: DJ workflow tool
projects.problem: DJs looking for tracks with strong low-end energy need information they can use in their existing music-library workflow. This tool connects bass analysis to RekordBox.
projects.role: I built a tool that profiles bass characteristics and writes the results directly into the RekordBox database.

decisions.purpose: Help DJs identify tracks with strong low-end energy.

decisions.decision: Results written into the RekordBox database
decisions.purpose: Put the analysis into the existing DJ workflow.

delivered: A bass-profiling tool with direct RekordBox database integration.

media.title: Bass analysis output
media.caption: The Bass Notes library view: a selected track’s low, mid, and high bass readings sit alongside its spectrum and the batch re-analysis queue.
media.alt: RekordBox Bass Notes desktop app showing a track library, bass scores, spectrum bars, and a batch re-analysis panel.

projects.contact: Need a custom tool to fit an existing workflow? Tell me where your data lives and how you want to use it.

projects.name: Dancefloor Bass Analyzer
projects.description: Only interested in your lower frequencies. Show me your music library and I’ll tell you what really hits.
projects.label: Desktop app / in development
projects.problem: A DJ exploring a music library needs a way to inspect the sub-sonic character of tracks. This project focuses on that exploration in a desktop interface.
projects.role: I’m developing the desktop app with React and Rust. Its focus is library exploration and track inspection, distinct from the direct RekordBox database integration of Bass Notes.

decisions.decision: A desktop interface built with React and Rust
decisions.purpose: Bring music-library exploration into a dedicated application.
Help DJs explore the sub-sonic characteristics of individual tracks.

delivered: An in-development desktop application. A downloadable production release is not being offered here.
planned: Continue developing and documenting local processing, track inspection, adjustable profiles, and responsive analysis. Exact feature readiness still needs confirmation.

media.title: Track library and detail view
media.caption: The in-development desktop app showing a scanned library, a selected track’s spectrum and spectrogram, and calculated sub-sonic measures.
media.alt: Dancefloor Bass Analyzer desktop app with a track list, audio spectrum, spectrogram, and bass-analysis measurements.

contentTodos: I’m gathering sound-system equipment information and audio-response metadata with a traveling DJ based in Baltimore. The goal is to build club-specific audio profiles that help DJs choose tracks likely to perform well on a given sound system.
projects.contact: Need a focused desktop tool for complex data? Tell me what you need to inspect and how you work with it.
